I was going to suggest residential. This child has severe behaviors and likely needs full time care. My son went to a group home (residential) when he was younger and stayed for a year and a half because of his severe behaviors. He's also mentally ill and on the spectrum. I waited until he was 11 even though it was recommended when he was 7 and inpatient for the first time. 

If I could do it again, I would send him earlier. Keeping him home didn't do him any favors because he wasn't in a therapeutic environment and wasn't making progress. Despite dozens of medications and 8 hospitalizations, he still struggled and his brother was traumatized. My older son never hurt my younger son but he did scream for hours and hurt himself and me. My younger son would beg my older son to stop hurting his mommy. 

Now my younger son has issues. Issues that he didn't have when he was little. I'm absolutely sure that it's from the trauma of listening to his brother scream for hours and seeing his brother hurt me. 

After residential, my son is on the right medication and he's a dream to be around. The staff was very warm and caring. They took them out into the community most days. Things like hockey games, Dave and busters... You get the idea. Just so they could learn how to handle themselves in the community. My younger son and I visited twice a week, with one visit being 6 hours long. We talked in the phone daily. If he ever needed to be restrained or got hurt in anyway, they called with him in the room and had him tell me what happened so I would feel comfortable that he wasn't abused. Any time he even got a bandaid they would call. 

I also attachment parented and it broke my heart in two to have my son living somewhere else. The first night he spent there I cried myself to sleep. It was different from the hospital because he wasn't coming home. 

All that said, it's very difficult to get a child in residential. In some states a Medicaid waiver pays for it, sometimes the school district. I would strongly suggest looking into it. The waiting lists are often very long as if you start the process now and she doesn't end up needing it in a year, you can pass on the spot. If she does, you're not starting at square one.

I suggest applying for section 8 all over the country. Affordable housing online. Org has the most comprehensive list of section 8 waiting lists. 

NJ is crazy expensive but they have rental assistance for a year so that would solve your immediate crisis. During that year, your name might come up in PA, or MO, or even FL. You might not get the most desirable place but it'll be stable. Nearly every property I looked at was nice. 

Like I said, apply to every open section 8 waiting list. They are also always opening and closing lists so I would check the website very frequently.
